_step150: the shot leaves on a tap's release (planning step 137): each tap goes down on `tick` and comes up on `release`, the next tick unless it says later
_about: 1-22 (level21), the designers' own solution, GOLD: 2 portals and all 5 crystals, medal 3 (planning step 218). It replaces the 4-portal route (medal 2) that was written around a port gap in the wall's first look; that route stays in git history.

Two breakable walls (719 at x 300 and 755 at x 332, y 99 to 225, side by side) shut the way to the door, and two destroyable stones (753 and 727) sit on a platform (x 70 to 234, top y 82) that the player, on the floor below it, cannot reach. So he is put on it:

a portal in the air over the platform's right end at (232, 60) (tap 40) and one on the player (tap 86, at (255, 205)): he lands on the platform. He walks left (92-283) behind stone 727, pushes it into stone 753 and takes the crystals along the platform; the stones roll off the left end onto the ramp and down it,

and he steps off after them past the crystal at (54, 98), walks the ramp and the floor and takes the last crystals. Each stone reaches a wall at about 3 m/s and breaks it, and a destroyable stone dies with the wall it breaks: 753 breaks wall 719 and 727 breaks wall 755. He walks right (314-) to the door. Won on tick 455.

WHY THIS WAS NOT A ROUTE BEFORE (the owner's report of 2026-11-05, 'the first ball destroys the wall, the second one just rams into the wall but does not destroy it'): the engine moves a body and then solves its contacts, and brakes a pair that stands inside the two bodies' travel in the step, so a stone that rolls at a wall ends the step 1 to 6 units from it with its velocity taken out; the wall's first look needed the stone within 1 unit (demolish.json contact.margin_px), so it never saw the contact at speed, and the creep that finally closed the gap read 0.1 m/s (the wall held).

Box2D takes the position first too and finds the pair touching at the START of the next step with the velocity the stone still carries, so the callback reads the stone at its roll speed. Demolish::State::Tick now reads a stone whose incoming approach reaches the wall within the step (the log says 'held short of the wall by the engine's brake'). Before it, 11 of 117 neighbours of this route won (the first tap's point scanned over x 226-238, y 56-64); now 115 do.

Margins (each input moved alone, all others kept; the units are ticks, or level units for a point): of 52 variants 50 still win and 35 still earn gold. The two that do not win: the second tap 8 ticks earlier (the shot is refused) and the first tap 8 ticks later (the second stone comes before the pair is placed). The 15 that win with medal 2 miss the crystal at (54, 98) on the way down: the walk's start 1 to 8 ticks later, the walk's end 2 to 20 earlier, the second tap 2 to 8 later or 4 earlier, the first tap's point 1 to 4 units right or 4 down.

NOT MEASURED ON THE ORIGINAL: that the original breaks the second wall with the stone at its roll speed (no clip shows a stone breaking a wall; the decode is ETHBeginContactCallback_breakable_wall #16-33 and Box2D's order, planning step 218). Nobody has done this by hand in this version.
